changes: p2 Jayakalyāṇa: removed 'commissioner' — the colophon gives only a genitive ('jayakalyāṇaviprasya ... tanmerutantraṃ'), which shows ownership, not that he had the copy made; kept 'owner', confidence lowered to medium; added the note that he was honoured by kings
p1: confidence lowered to medium; 'paḍmanārāyaṇakhaḥ' is probably a corruption of 'padmanārāyaṇākhyaḥ' ('named Padmanārāyaṇa')
date.nakshatra_yoga: vittarkṣa identified as Dhaniṣṭhā (vitta = dhana); 'nav saṃyute' left unexplained
date.year: still unresolved; added a note on a possible 'vyoma-bhūpa' reading
purpose: cleared — 'mokṣadaṃ' describes the text, not the purpose of copying

relations.evidence: jayakalyāṇaviprasya ... tanmerutantraṃ ... likhati hi gaṇakaḥ paḍmanārāyaṇakhaḥ

date.as_written: śāke vjo bhūpagate vatsare taiṣaśuklake || caturthyām indudivase vittarkṣa nav saṃyute

place.as_written: śrīman nepāladeśe paśupatinikaṭe vāṅmatīnimnagāyās tīre kāntipure

purpose: "copied for (or as the property of) the brahmin Jayakalyāṇa"
notes: "The Śaka year chronogram 'vjo bhūpa' is corrupt. 'vjo' might stand for vyoma (0) and 'bhūpa' is 16. But read right to left that gives an impossible Śaka 160, so a word is probably missing. No CE year is given for that reason. Taiṣa = Pauṣa. Moon in Dhaniṣṭhā on Pauṣa śukla 4 is astronomically plausible. 'nav saṃyute' is unclear: it may hide a yoga name or a number. The scribe's name 'paḍmanārāyaṇakhaḥ' (!) is probably 'padmanārāyaṇākhyaḥ'. Jayakalyāṇa is described as a brahmin honoured by kings ('nṛṇāṃ rājñāṃ saṃmānitasya'). The genitive marks the copy as his, but the colophon does not say outright that he commissioned it. Place: Kāntipura (Kathmandu), on the Bāgmatī near Paśupati."
